description.from:
As a reader and as a search engine, I want each language at a stable address, so existing English links never break and each language is found in its own language.

Design: urls.languages config with mode primaryAtRoot (existing sites; primary keeps today's URLs, others under a configured prefix) or prefixed (new sites only). The URL prefix is separate from the BCP 47 tag (recommended zh-Hans at /zh/). Translated slugs, frozen once published; slug changes use retire-with-redirect for that language. Every page carries hreflang for each published language in its group plus x-default, is canonical to itself, and per-language sitemaps join the sitemap index. A missing localization means no page in that language; the switcher and hreflang list only existing languages; Spanish listings list only Spanish Stories. A language goes public only when its interface strings are complete and reviewed. Publishing a localization re-renders its siblings (O(languages), coalesced). Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450).

Feature: Language addresses

Scenario: English stays at the root
  Given Machines on Machines with English primary at the root and Spanish at /es/
  When an English Story is published
  Then its address is unchanged from today and contains no /en/

Scenario: hreflang lists only languages that exist
  Given an English Story with a published Spanish localization and no Chinese one
  When either page is rendered
  Then both list hreflang en and es and x-default pointing at the English page
  And neither lists Chinese

Scenario: No English stand-in on a Spanish listing
  Given a Spanish section page
  When it is rendered
  Then it lists only Stories that have a published Spanish localization
description.to:
As a reader and as a search engine, I want each language at a stable address, so existing English links never break and each language is found in its own language.

Design: primaryAtRoot (existing sites; primary keeps today's URLs) or prefixed (new sites; '/' is a static redirect to the x-default home). The prefix is configured separately from the BCP 47 tag: Chinese is zh-Hans at /zh/ (Ryan's decision 1; /zh-hant/ possible later; never /cn/). Slugs (tentative, decision 7): translated and fixed once published for Latin-script languages; Chinese uses the primary's slug; ask Ryan again before Slice 2. hreflang for each published language plus x-default; self-canonical; one sitemap per language. Missing localization: no page; switcher and hreflang list only existing languages. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450), revised 2026-11-12 with Ryan's decisions.

Feature: Language addresses

Scenario: English stays at the root
  Given Machines on Machines with English at the root and Spanish at /es/
  When an English Story is published
  Then its address is unchanged from today and contains no /en/

Scenario: Chinese lives under /zh/ and declares Simplified script
  Given Chinese is configured with tag zh-Hans and prefix zh
  When a Chinese localization is published
  Then its address starts with /zh/ and the page declares lang zh-Hans

Scenario: hreflang lists only languages that exist
  Given an English Story with a published Spanish localization and no Chinese one
  When either page is rendered
  Then both list hreflang en and es and x-default pointing at the English page, and neither lists Chinese
